extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset of over 100K images with dense annotations of objects, attributes, relationships, region descriptions, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs, designed to enable cognitive scene understanding in computer vision. Each image has an average of 21 objects, 18 attributes, and 18 pairwise relationships, all canonicalized to WordNet synsets.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bernstein, Li Fei-Fei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Visual Genome was collected and verified entirely by crowd workers from Amazon Mechanical Turk. The pipeline involved multiple task stages for each component (region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, questions and answers). Various strategies were used to ensure accuracy and diversity, including majority voting and rapid judgments for verification.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 108,249 images from the intersection of MS-COCO's 328,000 images and YFCC's 100 million images, consisting of real-world, non-iconic images uploaded onto Flickr by users.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multi-stage crowdsourcing pipeline on Amazon Mechanical Turk covering region descriptions, objects (with bounding boxes requiring coverage and quality constraints), attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and QA pairs. Workers followed specific rules (e.g., 'seven Ws' for QA, diversity enforcement). Verification used majority voting (3 workers per annotation, majority must agree) and rapid judgments for objects.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Verification via majority voting (3 workers, majority must agree) and rapid judgments for objects. Canonicalization precision/recall evaluated on random samples of 200 items: Objects 88.0% precision / 98.5% recall; Attributes 85.7% precision / 95.9% recall; Relationships 92.9% precision / 88.5% recall.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 workers per annotation for verification (majority voting); 1 worker per region description for object extraction; 42 region descriptions per image on average
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk; no further demographic details provided
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford dependency parser (Manning et al., 2014) used to automatically extract nouns as suggestions for object annotation; Stanford NLP tools used to extract noun phrases for canonicalization; WordNet synset mapping for canonicalization of objects, attributes, and relationships
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased towards images of people, as the top synsets show sports-related and people-centric categories dominating the image distribution.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset covers only 972 WordNet synsets and is biased towards images of people and sports activities. Images were sourced from Flickr users, which may limit diversity of cultural and geographic representation.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains real-world images of people uploaded to Flickr, including images that may capture identifiable individuals in various activities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for use in visual understanding tasks including region description, question answering, scene graph generation, object detection, attribute recognition, and relationship detection.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and QAs are canonicalized (word sense disambiguated) by mapping to WordNet synsets. Stanford NLP tools are used to extract noun phrases, which are then mapped to their most frequent matching WordNet synset. Attributes are normalized via morphological stemming before mapping. Relationships exclude prepositions and are matched to WordNet sentence frames, with root hypernyms considered to reduce noise. Hand-crafted mapping rules (30 for objects, 15 for attributes, 20 for relationships) correct common failure cases. Mappings are verified via Amazon Mechanical Turk majority voting, and objects across region graphs are merged when bounding box overlap-over-union exceeds 0.8. Verification of annotations uses majority voting (3 workers, 2 must agree) and rapid judgments to remove vague, subjective, or incorrect labels.
